name: coderelay
description: Models can fail. Your task shouldn't. Resumes AI coding tasks across providers after mid-stream failures, without re-running side effects.
author: Bakul Labs

untrustedWorkspaces.description: CodeRelay writes files in the workspace and runs git to take rollback checkpoints, so it needs a trusted workspace. Ledgers from a previous session can be inspected once the workspace is trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: CodeRelay runs git as a child process and resolves real filesystem paths to fingerprint files, so it cannot operate on a virtual filesystem.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No tasks yet.
[Start a coding task](command:coderelay.startTask)
CodeRelay records every step to disk, so a task survives a provider failure — or a closed window.

Task ledgers belong to a project.
[Open a Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)
Open a folder or workspace and CodeRelay will keep its execution record alongside it.

No file changes yet.
Files the agent creates, edits or deletes appear here, with a diff against the checkpoint taken before the change.

Connect an AI provider.
[Add a Provider](command:coderelay.addProvider)
[Open Settings](command:coderelay.openSettings)

coderelay.providers.markdownDescription:
API endpoints CodeRelay may use. An endpoint is a configuration row rather than built-in support, so any OpenAI-compatible service — OpenRouter, NVIDIA, Azure OpenAI, a local server — works without a code change. See the [setup guide](https://github.com/BakulBd/CodeRelay#configuration).

**API keys are never stored here.** Use `CodeRelay: Add API Key`, which writes to the OS keychain through VS Code SecretStorage.

id.description: Your name for this endpoint. Keys are stored against it and it appears in the execution ledger, so it must be unique and stable.

kind.markdownDescription: The wire protocol, not the vendor. Use `openai` for anything that speaks Chat Completions, including OpenRouter, NVIDIA, Azure OpenAI, vLLM, Ollama and LM Studio.
enumDescriptions: OpenAI Chat Completions, and every service that speaks it.

baseUrl.markdownDescription: Origin and base path, without the endpoint suffix. For example `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, or `http://localhost:11434/v1`.

auth.markdownDescription: How the credential is presented. `bearer` sends `Authorization: Bearer`, `api-key-header` sends Azure OpenAI's `api-key` header, and `none` is for a local endpoint that does not authenticate.
enumDescriptions: Authorization: Bearer <key>. The default, and what most services expect.
No credential is sent. For a local endpoint; still needs a placeholder record from CodeRelay: Add API Key.

apiVersion.markdownDescription: The API version: a query parameter for Azure OpenAI, and a path segment for Gemini (for example `v1beta`). Pinned here so a new version does not need an extension release.

maxTokensField.markdownDescription: Which field carries the output cap, for `openai`-kind endpoints. Not guessable: newer OpenAI models require `max_completion_tokens` and reject `max_tokens`, while most gateways accept only `max_tokens`. Getting it wrong is a 400 on every attempt, which failover cannot route around. `none` omits the cap and lets the endpoint apply its own default.

headers.markdownDescription: Extra request headers, such as OpenRouter's `HTTP-Referer` and `X-Title`. **Never put a credential here** — this value is stored in plain settings.

coderelay.models.markdownDescription:
Models CodeRelay may route between, and what each one can do.

Capabilities are declared by you rather than guessed by the extension. Model line-ups change monthly, so a table shipped inside an extension goes stale and becomes a confident lie about a context window. CodeRelay records what it was told and gates failover on that — it never claims a model can do something.

model.description: The model id exactly as the endpoint expects it. For Azure OpenAI this is the deployment name.

contextWindow.description: Total input tokens the model accepts. Used to decide when to compact rather than overflow.

maxOutput.description: Maximum tokens the model may generate in one turn.

toolCalling.description: Whether this model can call tools. Required rather than assumed: guessing true sends tool definitions to a model that cannot use them, and guessing false silently hides the model from the router.

parallelToolCalls.description: Whether the model may request several tools in one turn.

reasoning.description: Whether the model reasons before answering, and whether that reasoning is visible in the stream.

costPerMTokIn.description: USD per million input tokens. Only used to break ties between otherwise equal failover targets.

coderelay.requireToolCalling.markdownDescription: Only route to models that can call tools. Every CodeRelay tool reads or writes files, so a model without tool calling cannot do the work — it can only narrate edits it never made. Turn this off only to use CodeRelay for read-only analysis.

coderelay.minContextWindow.description: Exclude models whose declared context window is smaller than this. 0 means no minimum.

coderelay.checkpoints.markdownDescription:
Snapshot the workspace with git before each file-modifying step, so any step can be inspected or reverted.

Safe to leave on. Snapshots are unreachable objects under `refs/coderelay/`, written through a private index. CodeRelay never touches `HEAD`, a branch, your staging area, or your working tree, and never creates a commit on a branch. Automatically inactive when the workspace is not a git repository.

coderelay.maxTurns.description: Stop a task after this many model turns. A backstop against a loop that makes no progress, not a quality setting.

coderelay.connectTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription:
Give up on an attempt if the provider has not sent response headers within this many seconds, and treat it as a transient failure that failover can route around.

Without a limit, an endpoint that accepts the connection and then never answers leaves the task waiting indefinitely — the one failure no retry policy can detect. `0` disables the limit, which is only sensible for a local endpoint.

coderelay.idleTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription:
Give up on an attempt if a response that had started streaming goes this many seconds without sending anything further.

Measured between chunks rather than over the whole response, and any traffic counts — including the keep-alive comments providers send while a model is still thinking — so a slow answer is not mistaken for a dead connection. Generous by default because a reasoning model can legitimately pause for a long time. `0` disables the limit.

coderelay.commands.markdownDescription:
Let the agent run shell commands in the workspace, so it can build, test, type-check and lint its own work.

Off by default. A command is the one tool whose effect CodeRelay cannot verify from the workspace afterwards, so turning this on is a deliberate choice rather than a default. When it is on, `#coderelay.permissionMode#` decides what runs without asking — and a destructive command asks in every mode.

coderelay.permissionMode.markdownDescription: How much the agent may run without asking. Only applies when `#coderelay.commands#` is on.
enumDescriptions: Read-only. Commands that could change anything are refused, not queued behind a prompt.
Ordinary development commands run. Anything irreversible asks first.
Everything runs except the irreversible shapes, which always ask.

coderelay.commandTimeoutMs.markdownDescription: How long a single command may run before it is killed, in milliseconds.

scripts.package: npm run clean && npm run typecheck && npm run test && npm run clean && npm run compile && vsce package --no-dependencies
scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run clean && npm run compile
